label: Heavy going
summary: Washington hardened its line on Iran: Vice President Vance said all options remain open and ruled out talks until attacks on Gulf shipping stop, while Tehran promised an "asymmetrical" response and said it is circumventing the US blockade. Ukraine struck a Russian vessel at Sochi and reported an oil depot hit; Germany pledged $290m to repair Ukraine's grid before winter. Nepal-China flood deaths passed 1,270 with hydropower workers still missing, and UNEP said the world will breach 1.5C within a few years. Ebola deaths in DR Congo topped 3,000, though the WHO expects vaccine trials by November. Markets rallied — the S&P 500 up 1.1% — but oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July. Brighter: Missouri's Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed House map and sent it to voters, and Pacific leaders closed their Palau forum with a climate declaration.
